Container.Name: FinTV
Container.Overview:
FinTV creates virtual 24/7 TV channels from the Jellyfin media library and delivers them as an HLS stream. This container is the FinTV service; it also serves the Jellyfin plugin.
Setup: 0. Before the first start, run these commands in the Unraid terminal: mkdir -p /mnt/user/appdata/fintv and chown 99:100 /mnt/user/appdata/fintv. The container runs as 99:100; otherwise Docker creates the directory as root and the service stops with "Applying database migrations failed" in the log. 1. Mount your media share under /media (read-only), start the container and check http://[IP]:8098/health. 2. In Jellyfin, go to Dashboard, Plugins, Repositories, add the repository http://[IP]:8098/plugin/manifest.json, install FinTV from the catalog and restart Jellyfin. 3. On the FinTV settings page in Jellyfin, enter the service URL (http://[IP]:8098) and click "Connect". Plugin and service set up their connection by themselves. 4. Tick your libraries and click "Sync now". The card "Paths" then shows for each library folder whether the service finds its files. If Jellyfin sees the media under the same path as this container, there is nothing to do. Otherwise enter the folder's path in this container (for example /media/movies) and click "Check and save". 5. Click "Set up Live TV" and create channels on the page "FinTV Channels".
Note: Click "Connect" right after the first start. Until then, anyone on the LAN who can reach the port can connect a plugin to the service. The plugin repository is reachable without a login; anyone on the LAN who can reach the port can download the plugin (it contains no secrets).
NVENC (optional, NVIDIA GPU): The Unraid plugin "Nvidia-Driver" must be installed. Add --runtime=nvidia under "Extra Parameters" (in addition to --user 99:100), set the variable FinTV__Streaming__Encoder to h264_nvenc and add the variables NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (GPU UUID or all) and NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,video,utility. The service checks the encoder at startup; if it cannot be used, it stops with an error message in the log.
Segments in RAM (optional): Add --tmpfs /transcode:mode=1777,size=1g under "Extra Parameters" (in addition to --user 99:100) and set "Streams base directory" to /transcode. The service then writes the stream segments into /transcode/streams instead of the appdata directory. The overview page in Jellyfin shows how much space the segments take.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Data directory (database, connection key, thumbnails, segments). Must be owned by 99:100.

Config.Name: Encoder
Config.Description: libx264 (CPU) or h264_nvenc (NVIDIA GPU, see the description).

Config.Name: Max. concurrent streams
Config.Description: Maximum number of streams running at the same time.

Config.Name: Streams base directory
Config.Description: Optional. Container path for the stream segments, e.g. a tmpfs mount in RAM (see the description). The service uses its subfolder streams. Empty = data directory.

Config.Name: Path mapping from (Jellyfin)
Config.Description: Optional; usually not needed. The card Paths on the FinTV settings page does the same. Path under which Jellyfin sees the media.

Config.Name: Path mapping to (container)
Config.Description: Optional; usually not needed. Path under which the service sees the media.

Config.Name: API key
Config.Description: Optional; leave empty. Only for a key set by hand (at least 32 characters), entered on the FinTV settings page under Manual setup.
